label: Lucius - Status Heartbeat
info:
Runs every 15 minutes (PLAN.md §15). Deliberately a fifth, dedicated flow rather than each sync flow pushing its own status inline — reads the HA helper entities the other three flows already maintain, computes one consolidated snapshot, pushes it to GoDaddy's new api/status_push.php (feeds status.php's HA/Node-RED/Analytics view), and writes the same snapshot to a new InfluxDB measurement (system_status_snapshot) per Ward's explicit request to keep it there for trend-watching.

UNTESTED, same caveat as the other three flows — PLUS one piece of real, deliberate scope-narrowing worth knowing about: PLAN.md §15 suggested this flow also query HA's own /api/config for HA version/uptime, to give the 'HA' category more than just a heartbeat. That's NOT implemented here — it would need either a Supervisor API token or a manually-managed long-lived access token, neither of which this project otherwise needs, and guessing at that auth mechanism without confirming it against a real HA instance felt like exactly the kind of unverified assumption this project has been burned by before (see PLAN.md §2's require('fs') and /config lessons). Instead, the 'ha' category's only component (ha_core) uses this heartbeat's own successful execution as the signal — which is still real signal: if HA/Node-RED goes down, this flow stops running, ha_core goes overdue on status.php, and that overdue state IS the answer to 'is HA up.' Richer HA-native detail is a clearly flagged open follow-up, not a silent gap.

Also unverified: the 12 chained api-current-state nodes reading the other flows' helper entities via outputProperties (valueType 'entityState') — a reasonable, standard use of this palette's read capability, but this project has only used it for WRITES (api-call-service) so far, never reads.
